page.apps.intro: Apps that ship with Windows and that most people never open. Only apps installed on this PC are listed, and anything you remove can be brought back with Revert.
page.ads.intro: Switches off the places where Windows shows promotions, suggestions and tips.
page.edge.intro: Stops Microsoft Edge from starting on its own and blocks the Widgets feed. Edge itself stays installed, because parts of Windows need it.
page.look.intro: A plain picture on the lock screen and desktop, without rotating content or tips.
page.onedrive.intro: Removes OneDrive without losing files. Read the description before you tick it.
page.history.intro: Earlier runs on this PC. Revert puts a run's settings back the way they were and brings back the apps it removed.
page.settings.intro: Language, appearance and information about this tool.
page.empty: Everything on this page is already done or not present on this PC.

item.ads.promoted-apps.title: Stop Windows installing promoted apps
item.ads.promoted-apps.desc: Windows can quietly install apps it wants to promote and pin them to Start. This turns that off.
item.ads.start-suggestions.title: No app suggestions in Start
item.ads.start-suggestions.desc: Removes the recommended apps and promotions from the Start menu.
item.ads.account-nags.title: No account reminders in Start
item.ads.account-nags.desc: Stops the Start menu from pushing Microsoft 365, OneDrive backup and sign-in reminders.
item.search.bing.title: No web results in Start search
item.search.bing.desc: Start search only looks at this PC. Part of this is a policy, so Settings may say it is managed by your organisation.
item.ads.tips.title: No tips and welcome screens
item.ads.tips.desc: Turns off tips, tricks and the welcome experience that appears after updates.
item.ads.finish-setup.title: No "finish setting up your device" screen
item.ads.finish-setup.desc: Stops the full-screen reminder that asks you to finish setting up Microsoft services.
item.ads.suggested-notifications.title: No suggested notifications
item.ads.suggested-notifications.desc: Stops Windows from sending notifications that suggest features and apps.
item.ads.settings-suggestions.title: No suggestions in Settings
item.ads.settings-suggestions.desc: Removes suggested content from the Settings app.
item.ads.explorer.title: No ads in File Explorer
item.ads.explorer.desc: Stops OneDrive and Microsoft 365 promotions inside File Explorer.
item.ads.advertising-id.title: Turn off the advertising ID
item.ads.advertising-id.desc: Apps can no longer use your advertising ID to show personalised ads.
item.ads.tailored.title: No tailored experiences
item.ads.tailored.desc: Windows stops using diagnostic data to personalise tips and ads.
item.edge.autostart.title: Stop Edge starting with Windows
item.edge.autostart.desc: Removes the entry that launches Edge in the background when you sign in.
item.edge.startup-boost.title: Turn off Edge startup boost
item.edge.startup-boost.desc: Edge no longer preloads itself at sign-in. Set as a policy.
item.edge.background.title: Stop Edge running in the background
item.edge.background.desc: Edge closes fully when you close its window. Set as a policy.
item.widgets.block.title: Block Widgets
item.widgets.block.desc: Turns off the Widgets board and its taskbar button. Set as a policy, so Settings may say it is managed by your organisation.
item.widgets.lockscreen.title: No widgets on the lock screen
item.widgets.lockscreen.desc: Removes weather, news and other cards from the lock screen. Set as a policy.
item.look.lock-tips.title: No tips on the lock screen
item.look.lock-tips.desc: Removes fun facts, tips and promotions from the lock screen.
item.look.lock-spotlight.title: Plain lock screen picture
item.look.lock-spotlight.desc: Turns off Windows Spotlight and sets the standard Windows picture.
item.look.desktop-default.title: Standard desktop picture
item.look.desktop-default.desc: Sets the standard Windows 11 picture as the desktop background.
item.gaming.gamebar-popups.title: Stop Game Bar pop-ups
item.gaming.gamebar-popups.desc: Use this if you remove Xbox Game Bar. Without it, games can show an error pop-up that asks for an app to open Game Bar links.
item.onedrive.remove.title: Remove OneDrive and move folders back
item.onedrive.remove.desc: Downloads files that exist only online, copies Desktop, Documents and Pictures back to their normal folders, uninstalls OneDrive and points Windows at the normal folders. Your files on onedrive.com are not touched. The old OneDrive folder is left in place for you to check and delete.
note.app.bing-search: Puts web results into Start search.
note.app.widgets: The Widgets board and its news feed.
note.app.outlook: Remove it if you read mail somewhere else.
note.app.teams: Remove it if you do not use Teams.
note.app.copilot: The Copilot app. Remove it if you do not use it.
note.app.m365: The Microsoft 365 launcher, not Word or Excel themselves.

note.app.xbox: The Xbox and Game Pass app.
note.app.game-bar: The Win+G overlay. If you remove it, also tick "Stop Game Bar pop-ups".
note.app.xbox-services: Some games from Microsoft need these to sign in to Xbox.
